item.title: Verification Is Not Knowledge: Science needs more than answers (205 pts)
item.description:
URL: https://blog.cosmos-institute.org/p/verification-is-not-knowledge, See on Hacker News

This is a guest essay by Jessica Hullman, Ginni Rometty Professor of Computer Science and Policy Fellow at Northwestern University.

In his essay on the role that rigorous proofs play in mathematical advances, Bill Thurston writes that the measure of success in math research is “whether what we do enables people to understand and think more clearly and effectively about mathematics.” Many recent discussions of AI for science hinge on a tension between understanding and answers. Is science about humans achieving insight, or the archiving of verifiable solutions?

One side prioritizes outputs. Progress is implied to be evident in verifiable proofs of longstanding conjectures and cures for diseases, whether humans were involved in their making or not. The other side argues that human understanding is paramount, because it drives integration of new findings into the canon, because it shapes and inspires the next generation, and so on. But the first side, those who emphasize correct outputs, dismisses this as gatekeeping or nostalgia.

When Terry Tao posed a thought experiment in a recent talk, asking how comfortable people would be taking a cancer treatment produced by AI, complete with a formal certificate of correctness and a passed phase 3 trial, but without any human understanding how it was found, critics suggested that Tao’s reasoning missed the point. Of course a patient with stage 4 cancer would welcome the treatment.

Other examples concern ambiguity in authorship. Tom Dietterich wrote about arXiv’s growing problem with papers submitted by human authors who seem unlikely to have the expertise to understand the claims. Many questioned in response why accountability – by which I mean being answerable for a claim, able to describe what it rests on and respond when it’s challenged – should matter if verification has been solved. I suggested peer reviewers reserve their expert judgment for texts that don’t get flagged as heavily AI-written, so as to prioritize review as human exchange, but some see this as an obstruction to truth-seeking rather than an attempt to preserve it.

The problem is that if we all agree that outputs matter–that we do care about the solutions to longstanding conjectures, that we do ultimately want to know how to cure diseases–then understanding appears as something separate. It’s cast as a mental state that looks optional next to the cure or the proof itself, and becomes easy to dismiss as a second-order constraint that we tack on because historically we’ve required it to arrive at the solutions in the first place.

When defenders of understanding don’t dispute this separation, they immediately lose the argument. It becomes easy for the side that prioritizes output to peg them as simply not trying hard enough to envision a new future. But the superficial framing of understanding that we keep falling back on obscures deeper concerns that these examples share. They are less about anyone’s mental state than about what happens when something goes wrong. Tao’s scenario turns on the possibility that the AI passed the trial by exploiting a weakness in the trial itself. A paper whose authors can’t explain its claims leaves no one to consult if those claims fail.

Where along the way did we come to believe that scientific value lies in correctness alone?

This intuition is ultimately less about AI than it appears. The inclination to let AI drive science is less a sign of how forward-thinking one is about our future with AI, and more a symptom of a “value-free ideal” that has shaped our thinking since the Cold War era: a view that only epistemic criteria (not ethical and social values) deserve a place in judging what the evidence shows. That it pervades our debates about AI for science is not so surprising; it’s only in the last few decades or so that rejecting the value-free ideal became the philosophical mainstream.

This ideal feeds unrealistic expectations and keeps us from seeing that pushback against the rapid infiltration of AI output into the scientific record is neither anti-AI nor anti-science. The stakes are bigger than any one debate or field. The value-free ideal distorts how we go about seeking truth, causing us to mistake verified results for knowledge. It threatens the human capacities that sustain science, causing us to see criticism and accountability as inconvenient overhead rather than the mechanics of knowledge production. It leaves us confused about what understanding is, and consequently why it matters.

The social contract for science represents an idealized relationship between science and society that arose after World War II in the US: scientists receive public funding and autonomy, and in return society receives the benefits of their inquiry. Built on a distinction between pure and applied science and a “linear model” in which basic research feeds applied work, the social contract replaces abstract arguments about the value of understanding with practical societal benefits, reshaping how we see science. Drawing on arguments made by concerned scientists in the late 1800s, who worried public celebration of new inventions like electric lights and the steam engine would crowd out respect for what they viewed as their more essential contributions, it also helped to forge a value-free ideal that says that at its core, science must be removed from “contextual values” like ethical or social concerns. For the social contract to gain broad societal buy-in as a model of scientific progress (and consequently shore up government investment in scientific research), we needed to imagine truth-seeking as the impersonal application of methods, immune to political or social pressures.

Philosophers of science aspired to inquiry based only on “epistemic” (or “cognitive”) values. Any influence from the scientist’s intentions or values came to be seen as a risk that the right methods should minimize, laying the groundwork for today’s questions about why it should matter who asserted the claim so long as it’s correct.

Many debates about AI’s role in science come down to disagreements about whether the scientific truth can be realized purely through use of the right procedures. Over the course of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, there was almost a moralizing drive to eliminate as much of the scientist’s self as possible from the scientific process, so that trust in individuals could be replaced with trust in the system.

AI agents set loose on the scientific literature, able to verify and intervene experimentally themselves, look like the long-awaited fulfillment of nineteenth century scientific ethics. Much of the “AI for science” rhetoric inherits what I call the “science is naturally aligned” premise: by enacting the scientific method at scale, with its various justification procedures, we can reach a place where we no longer need human judgment to produce truth.

Is what is true really so separable from understanding or accountability? Math has become a centerpiece in recent debates because it gives us a case where correctness can be separated cleanly; a proof can be verified by AI without any human understanding how it works. What mathematicians still want after verification is a clue to what mechanical objectivity can’t provide.

Philosophers of science now predominantly reject the value-free ideal as being appropriate or helpful. Values enter because whether we reject or accept hypotheses is contingent on how we weigh consequences. Even in abstract realms like math, there are often simply too many possible truths for values not to be brought to bear in sifting through them. Mathematicians accepted long ago that in principle a machine can enumerate the set of theorems that can be proved from a given set of axioms. Yet the scale of this space is immense, motivating people to seek clever shortcuts for exploring it.

But even with automated theorem-proving at scale, not all theorems are equally interesting to people. Values are inherent in the choices that lead to certain open problems gaining widespread appeal, and in the processes by which the community comes to accept and internalize the results. Fermat’s Last Theorem initially got attention not because it was an inherently important conjecture, but because Fermat claimed to have a proof but never provided it, enticing others to try their hand. It became central when it was shown that it would follow from the modularity conjecture, which proposed a previously unanticipated link between disparate areas of math. It was considered solved after peer review exposed an error that led to a corrected version of the original proof, even though formal verification didn’t come until recently. Epistemic taste develops because without it, we face an undifferentiated flood of facts. Taste is a capacity we develop over time as we choose problems, pursue some of them, and see which yield new understanding or ideas.

If AI takes over choosing, we risk losing the personal fulfillment and community cooperation that motivates many to want to develop a capacity for scientific judgment in the first place. Tao makes a similar point by framing open problems as lighthouses rather than destinations. Reaching them prematurely with AI may sterilize the field around them. If, as fields are transformed by AI, we stop producing people who can judge what’s interesting and aligned with human aspirations, we may end up with a science that fails to serve basic human interests. Its results will consume attention from those to whom it is targeted, while providing neither fodder for subsequent discoveries nor contributing to the processes that help shape the next generation.

This starts to sound like motivation for a new kind of linear model for science, which ensures that human reflection and inquiry are sustained despite AI becoming better than the average mathematician. The risk of proceeding without human intervention is drift, as anyone who relies heavily on agents to carry out their work knows. Even when you think you’re providing a well-specified pipeline for implementing and verifying an idea, it’s easy to end up mired in nuance in some branch you never expected to traverse. When you don’t assert epistemic agency, you can easily end up with a “view from nowhere” – not a form of pure objectivity, but an answer without a corresponding question. Maintaining alignment is not a problem you solve once and move on from. It requires a supply of humans who can articulate and adjudicate between values.

Mechanical objectivity attempted to replace trust in individuals with trust in procedures, but that substitution has never happened as intended. To understand why, we need to look at the interactions that truth-seeking depends on.

There’s a tendency to see the social aspects of science as opposed to rationality. The social side of science can produce pathologies, like bad conventions, herd behavior, or deference to prestige. But scientific knowledge as we know it has always been the product of many epistemic agents bringing values and expertise to bear, and revising their views in response to challenge, not from some external verifying engine.

As the philosopher Helen Longino argues, the basis for objective public knowledge is a shared language and a belief that things we describe exist independently of how we perceive them. If we can agree on descriptions of the world, then two things become possible: we can defer to others’ experiences to obtain knowledge, and meaningfully criticize scientific claims.

Scientific communities develop shared standards and vocabulary that allow us to build on one another’s findings. We don’t need to verify everything firsthand, and sometimes relying on others’ findings can give us better grounds for believing something than investigating it ourselves, particularly when they possess evidence or expertise that we lack.

Without criticism, we cannot have objectivity; it is, as Longino puts it “dependent upon the depth and scope of the transformative interrogation that occurs in any given scientific community.” For criticism to be transformative requires someone who is obliged to take it up.

Practices like peer review and post-publication critique are not just fact-checks for sifting out false positives – they are about members of the community holding one another to the commitments that their assertions imply, and negotiating where to draw the line on the influence of personal preference. As Longino explains, “[t]he function of peer review is not just to check that the data seem right and the conclusions well-reasoned, but to bring to bear another point of view on the phenomena, whose expression might lead the original author(s) to revise the way they think about and present their observations and conclusions.”

Method itself is best understood as a social process, where progress depends on how well a community sustains critical dialogue. This dialogue builds the people in it, shaping what it means for them to understand and exercise judgment along with the knowledge it produces.

If criticism and an ability to trust others’ assertions are integral to the production of knowledge, we might ask whether AI can fulfill these same functions. Can models realize transformative criticism without human involvement? Can we trust the assertions of AI agents without obtaining direct understanding ourselves? And if we do, what happens to our own capacity to question, criticize, and stand behind results?

The view that it shouldn’t matter who asserted some result as long as it’s correct corresponds to reliabilist epistemologies in philosophy. Classical epistemology insisted that true beliefs are only knowledge if the believer is able to produce reasons for their belief. In contrast, reliabilist epistemologies argue that true beliefs can, at least in some cases, represent genuine knowledge even when the believer can’t produce justifying reasons, provided they arrived at those beliefs by exercising capacities that are reliable producers of true beliefs in those circumstances.

But there are limits to what reliability can provide. The philosopher Robert Brandom imagines a community where the members hold true beliefs, which they have acquired through reliable means, but cannot offer reasons for any of them. Because attributing reliability to the source of their beliefs would itself provide a form of justification based on inference, the community can’t know that they are reliable. They are reliable as instruments indicating something about their surroundings, but unable to recognize themselves as such. Unable to even possess the concept of reliability, Brandom concludes, they cannot have knowledge.

If reliability alone can’t produce knowledge, what can? Brandom’s response is that calling something knowledge is a social act. To call what someone has “knowledge,” we have to attribute to them a commitment (that they believe that thing) along with an entitlement to that belief (that it is justified). But we also have to undertake that commitment ourselves, in the sense that we endorse the belief.

The scientist who first asserted the claim allows us to repeat the claim (and draw conclusions from it) while leaving them responsible for justifying it if challenged. We do this relatively easily in human science because if it turns out there was something wrong with the original assertion, there is an answerable source we can consult to resolve it. Assertions have social significance because we can hold the original author accountable for what was said. This is the sense of understanding that matters most for science, that mathematicians want after the proof has been verified, and that Tao’s patient wants too: results that can be interrogated and reconceptualized where needed, to avoid the perception of progress that fails to serve our goals.

But when we rely on AI results we don’t understand, there is only the person whose name is on the result to turn to. This is the problem arXiv is concerned with: no author can take responsibility for what they cannot understand, and hence they cannot respond to criticism by saying what it rests on, or whether it should be withdrawn. In other words, formal authorship survives while substantive authorship weakens. And so we lose the potential for transformative criticism, which is what sustains our notions of “objective” results in the first place.

A natural question is whether we could put the criticism to the AI agent itself, letting it decide whether to defend the result or concede and revise. What would it mean for AI to be an epistemic agent capable of committing to its assertions?

There are a few challenges with today’s agents that would need to be overcome. One is their lack of persistence and identity in the sense that we attribute it to people. An agent that retracts something it asserted in one session is not bound to maintain its correction or the reasoning behind it in the next. If each new result is produced by a new bespoke multi-agent infrastructure, it becomes hard to “keep score” in the way that naturally happens within networks of human scientists.

Scientific knowledge production depends on epistemic agents who have something at stake. Making bad claims changes the scientist’s standing in the community, which is how trust in individuals can remain calibrated. It’s not clear what comparable loss an AI agent faces in retracting its assertions, particularly given its lack of persistence.

To overcome such limitations would require a considerable shift in how we develop AI: away from being maximally helpful in each exchange and toward being accountable across them, as human scientists tend to be. This may well be possible. But I don’t think accountable AI will be enough to sustain meaningful science from our human perspective.

Let’s say we succeed in developing agents that can answer for claims. This is half of what accountability demands, but we also need others capable of holding them accountable, by asking for evidence, questioning assumptions, recognizing when an answer is evasive. Endorsements of others’ assertions are only as good as our capacity to engage with what we are endorsing.

These are capacities that get built by exercising them, by choosing problems, defending our work, reviewing papers, challenging others’ results. When we don’t exercise our capacities, we lose them. It’s not clear what we gain from a perfectly accountable AI if no one can judge how good its answers are. We’d have truth-seeking in theory, but no one who is able to do it.

Thurston’s notion of mathematical success points to this shared capacity to interrogate, extend, and repair a field’s knowledge that he’s hinting at. As he puts it, “As long as people in the field are comfortable that the idea works, it doesn’t need to have a formal written source.” Verification can tell us a result checks out in a technical sense, but only a community of people prepared to stand behind it can turn it into knowledge.

If we continue to appeal to value-free ideals that frame correctness as all that matters, we will keep building tools that prioritize answers while neglecting the truth-seeking and understanding of the people who can make them count.

Cosmos Institute is the Academy for Philosopher-Builders, technologists building AI for human flourishing. We run fellowships, fund fast prototypes, and host seminars with institutions like Oxford, Aspen Institute, and Liberty Fund.

item.title: Kitty 0.50 (343 pts)
item.description:
URL: https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/changelog/#, See on Hacker News

kitty is a feature-rich, cross-platform, fast, GPU based terminal. To update kitty, follow the instructions.

Detailed list of changes¶

0.50.0 [2026-11-03]¶

  • Allow docking kitty windows to the edges of other windows or of the tab, for status bars, file trees, etc. Create them with launch --type=window-dock or launch --type=tab-dock, see Docked windows

  • A new option restore_session_after_logout to save the state of every kitty instance, including scrollback, when logging out, restarting or shutting down and restore it the next time kitty starts. On macOS, the state is encrypted with a key in the keychain. On Linux, it requires the Inhibit desktop portal. See Restoring kitty after logging out (#1197, #10659)

  • Allow using tabs like named workspaces: A new launch --focus-existing option to focus an existing window or tab instead of creating a new one, a new by-title value for launch --location to keep tabs in alphabetical order and new options for kitten @ detach-window and the detach_window action to send windows to a named tab, creating it if needed (#10627)

  • Wayland: The client side window decorations used on compositors such as GNOME now look like native GNOME decorations and follow the desktop titlebar font, text scaling, button layout and titlebar click action settings (#10766)

  • Wayland: Support touchscreens. A tap is a click, a finger that moves scrolls with momentum, and a finger held still before it moves selects text (#5432, #10551)

  • Custom shaders: New cursor-trail-railgun, cursor-trail-torpedo and cursor-trail-pixiedust shaders that make particles fly off the cursor as it moves, in the style of neovide. Shaders can now be controlled with key presses via the new shader_event action (see Controlling shaders with key presses), can be faded in and out, reversed and looped with new animation_* pipeline directives and can define a pointer_map() function so that clicks and selections land on the text shown under the mouse, which the crt shader now uses, see Shaders that move content. Also fix animations becoming jerky after kitty has been running for a few hours, shaders specified by path not being found and various pipeline bugs (#10587, #10667, #10693, #10595, #10694, #10639)

  • Graphics protocol: Add two new indexed color image formats whose pixels are indices into the terminal color palette, so that images change color along with the color scheme, and allow clients to detect support for individual protocol features, such as animation and Unicode placeholders, via the new e query key, see Querying support for protocol features (#9379, #10732)

  • Support the Program Status Protocol (OSC 7501) that lets programs report whether they are working, finished, failed or blocked waiting on the user. Shown in the tab bar via a new tab.program_status field for tab_title_template, see Reporting the status of a program

  • Automatic color themes: When the system switches between light and dark, keep colors set by programs running in a window, by the ssh kitten, by launch --color or launch --copy-colors, and use the current theme colors when a program restores its saved colors. launch --color colors now also survive config reloads. The ssh kitten can use different color schemes for remote hosts in dark and light mode via the new kitten-ssh.color_scheme_dark, kitten-ssh.color_scheme_light and kitten-ssh.color_scheme_no_preference options (#10724)

  • Layouts: Align the borders of neighboring windows and keep the gaps between them uniform, and add a new option collapse_window_margins to have the margins of neighboring windows collapse into each other instead of adding up (#10508)

  • Window resizing: A new --strategy=edge mode to select and move a specific internal divider in the Splits layout, and hold Alt with a resize letter to take a fraction of the remaining resize steps, configurable with the new --fraction option

  • Scale the thickness of box drawing characters, cursors and the window title bar border with the font size, so they no longer look too thin when zoomed in or too thick when zoomed out. At the configured font_size nothing changes (#10362)

  • mouse_map can now map the scroll wheel, via the wheel_up, wheel_down, wheel_left and wheel_right buttons, for example, to change the font size with Ctrl+scroll

  • A new option hyperlink_target_position to control where the URL shown by show_hyperlink_targets is displayed, including as a browser style tooltip next to the mouse cursor (#10770)

  • Show the hand pointer and hover highlighting over links only when the pressed modifiers match a configured mouse action for opening the link with a single click, updating immediately when modifiers are pressed or released

  • quick-access-terminal kitten: New kitty +kitten quick_access_terminal --if-running, kitty +kitten quick_access_terminal --listen-on and kitty +kitten quick_access_terminal --hold options to run programs in an already running quick access terminal, use a fixed remote control socket and keep the terminal open after the program exits (#10603)

  • Sessions: A new os_window_position keyword and a new --os-window-geometry option for save_as_session to save the size, position and state of OS Windows in session files. Also fix the OS Window size and os_window_title in sessions sometimes being ignored (#10675)

  • Command palette: Show action and kitten aliases at the top when the search query is empty, so they can be used to pin frequently used actions (#10711)

  • Vertical tab bars: When tab_title_max_length is set, size the tab bar to fit the decorations of the current tab_bar_style, allowing much narrower tab bars (#10680)

  • Linux/BSD: Detect MIME types for open actions and kittens using the shared-mime-info cache, matching the rest of the desktop, including files without an extension, such as Makefile, and MIME type aliases (#3056)

  • IME: Keep the candidate window anchored at the start of the pre-edit text and at the cursor, so it no longer jumps around while composing text. On macOS, commit in-progress IME or dictation text instead of discarding it when the OS window loses focus (#10642, #10644)

  • Shell integration: Make the kitty terminfo files available in commands run via run0, similar to sudo (#10692)

  • kitty --config=NONE now also skips the automatic color theme files, open-actions.conf, launch-actions.conf, mime.types, paste-actions.py, notifications.py and the custom window icon in the kitty config directory

  • Processes kitty inserts to wrap the program it runs, such as /usr/bin/login on macOS or the wrapper for launch --hold, are now skipped when reporting the pid, working directory, command line and environment of a window in kitten @ ls and when matching windows. Also fix launch --cwd=root using the working directory of the foreground process instead of the root process while the shell is running a command

  • Nightly builds now show the date and hash of the commit they were built from in the output of kitty --version and kitten --version

  • Do not render between render frames to reduce flicker from programs that draw with many small partial updates (#10749)

  • Performance: Faster growing of the GPU sprite cache, particularly on macOS, less CPU usage with a non-zero input_delay and no continuous re-rendering when a selection is present and the window is scrolled back (#10714)

  • Remote control: Fix a crafted request being able to bypass password based remote control authentication by masquerading as a cancellation of an asynchronous request

  • Remote control: Fix many commands, including action, send-key, set-colors, set-background-opacity, set-font-size, ls, run and set-enabled-layouts, ignoring options, reporting false success or silently misinterpreting invalid input, particularly when used in remote_control mappings. set-colors now parses color files the same way as kitty.conf. Also fix a single unresponsive peer blocking all remote control communication and a crash when using damaged images with set-window-logo or set-background-image (#10672, #10632, #10688, #10690, #10715)

  • Fix various terminal emulation bugs, including in origin mode cursor position reports, erasing multicell characters, the CHT escape code and copying text containing tabs, wide characters being drawn on the wrong row after colliding with scaled text, emoji sequences being split into multiple cells when wrapped, text typed into a new window before the program is ready sometimes being garbled, as well as a heap buffer overflow, an out of bounds write and a use-after-free when reloading the config (#10609, #10729, #10632, #10682, #10767)

  • Graphics protocol: Allow shared memory object names without a leading slash again, for sandboxed macOS applications, and fix various bugs with animation frames and Unicode placeholders (#10684, #10599, #10632)

  • Fix various window and tab management bugs, with focus moving to the wrong window on close, drag and drop onto title bars, visual window selection, Grid layout placement, title bar padding and tab titles being truncated too early. detach_tab now shows custom titles in the OS Window chooser (#10640)

  • Fix render jitter when scrolled back with a partial line and the client is using the synchronised rendering escape code (#10794)

  • Fix bold or italic Nerd Font icons sometimes being rendered using glyphs from an unrelated font, the cursor trail not always being shown when focus moves to a different window, watcher entries not being removed on config reload and changing text marker colors at runtime, for example with kitten @ set-colors or automatic theme switching, applying the colors of each marker to the next one (#10591)

  • ssh kitten: Preserve the permissions of copied directories, fix copying files outside HOME whose paths share its prefix and files in HOME being copied to an absolute path with --symlink-strategy=resolve when HOME is a symlink, fix hanging when re-using a shared connection that has silently died and fix colors 16-255 being set to white with themes that do not define them (#10691, #10661, #10727, #10737)

  • Desktop UI kitten: Fix D-Bus activation when kitten is installed in a path containing spaces or quoting characters (#10784)

  • Automatic color themes: Stop using cached colors and background images after the corresponding theme file has been deleted and apply theme files created after kitty was started when reloading the config (#10786)

  • Themes kitten: Fix overwriting the Unicode input kitten’s recent entries and input mode, and vice versa, by using separate caches (#10780)

  • Remote file kitten: Preserve the local edited copy and show its recovery path when the final upload fails, including when the SSH connection has died (#10789)

  • Transfer kitten: When receiving files, replace existing symbolic and hard links at the destination instead of overwriting the files they point to, and write to a temporary file that is renamed into place, so an interrupted transfer no longer leaves a truncated file behind (#10713)

  • Drag and drop kitten: Reject copying or moving a directory into itself or one of its subdirectories, and moving a directory into a symlink that points inside it, which would delete the moved files. When moving, do not delete sources that were replaced during the drop, for example by files merged through a symlink in the destination. Respect overwrite confirmation for case and Unicode equivalent names on filesystems that treat them as aliases, list the existing files that will be overwritten under their actual names, including inside symlinked directories, and fix dropping a directory over an existing file. No longer rename remotely dropped files whose names differ only in case on case sensitive filesystems (#10769, #10772)

  • Drag and drop protocol: Fix base64 data with padding at the end being rejected, as allowed by the protocol (#10777)

  • Clipboard kitten: Fix only the last of several outputs that use the same MIME type being saved, for example with kitten clipboard -g picture.png picture.jpg, the data is now downloaded and decoded only once for all such outputs. Reject duplicate output files, including ones that differ only in case on case-insensitive filesystems or whose paths contain a symlink followed by ... Fix a race when replacing an existing output file, losing the original file if writing it fails and kitten clipboard -g -m . formats.txt silently doing nothing. Also preserve the permissions of and follow symlinks at existing output files (#10738, #10744)

  • Kittens: When saving files, such as themes, config files or clipboard output, write to the target of a symlink even when the target does not yet exist, instead of replacing the symlink with a regular file (#10740)

  • Kittens: Fix laggy mouse selection and failures comparing remote directories in the diff kitten, Unicode quotes not being removed from around paths and URLs in the hints kitten, the order of styles with negative or closely spaced fractional axis values in the choose-fonts kitten, various bugs in the choose-files, quick-access-terminal and other kittens and reject command-line options missing their required value (#10634, #10641, #10676, #10687, #10730)

  • Wayland: Fix a crash on compositors without cursor-shape support, kitty being disconnected by GNOME when showing a long covered window, the app_id being lost when hiding and showing windows, kitty --os-window-tag not setting the window tag and various drag and drop bugs (#10597, #10602, #10604, #10759, #10632)

  • Linux: Fix momentum scrolling up or left, X11 wheel events from sources without smooth scrolling being ignored and various desktop notification bugs. Notifications now identify kitty’s desktop file, so desktops such as KDE can group them (#10625, #10695, #10610, #10721)

  • macOS: Fix padding rendering black after sleep, OS windows not staying on all spaces, a duplicate path when dropping items from Apple Mail, emoji from a monochrome emoji font such as Noto Emoji not using the foreground color, a memory leak, reloading config causing Apple injected shortcuts to not work and kitty freezing when opening a new window while another entry in /dev is stuck (#10708, #10581, #10628, #10673, #10741, #10757, #10793)

  • zsh: Respect the user’s descriptions format style for completion group headings, fixing literal %B markers appearing with fzf-tab, and fix a “maximum nested function level reached” error at every prompt after interrupting a command run at shell startup, for example via a session file (#10748, #10768)

0.49.2 [2026-10-01]¶

  • Fix reverse-video extra cursors to use the color type encoded by the multiple-cursors protocol.

  • Make reverse-video cursors follow dimmed text colors while keeping text under block cursors legible.

  • A new option detect_url_regex to detect arbitrary text, such as file references in compiler output, as clickable URLs under the mouse (#10407)

  • Reduce input latency by processing small amounts of program output, such as the echo of typed characters, immediately instead of waiting for input_delay (#10560)

  • Drag and drop: Restore the previously active tab after dropping a dragged tab on the same OS window’s tab bar, even if it was reordered after a hover switch

  • Drag and drop: Fix an out of bounds memory access when parsing a URI list sent by a remote client that does not end with a newline (#10618)

  • Sessions: Expand launch option variables when an option value matches the command name

  • Preserve transparent background colors when applying unrelated launch color overrides

  • ssh kitten: Preserve SSH option values following a spaced --kitten option

  • Fix a memory leak when loading a corrupt PNG image that has an embedded ICC color profile

  • Custom shaders: The builtin dim-inactive-windows shader no longer dims the tab bar and the padding, border and margin around the active window (#10524)

  • Custom shaders: The builtin northern-lights shader is now about twice as fast. Its MARCH_STEPS setting can now be lowered to trade a little quality for even more speed on slower GPUs

  • Custom shaders: A new cursor-trail-motion-blur shader that makes the cursor trail glide smoothly during fast cursor movements

  • Vertical tabs: Improve rendering of tabs when using the powerline tab_bar_style

  • Graphics: Fix images briefly disappearing for one frame the first time an image is replaced during a synchronized update (#10538)

  • X11: Fix copy and paste targeting the wrong OS window when the keyboard focus is set to PointerRoot or None

  • diff kitten: Fix freezes and very high memory use when a very long line, such as in a minified file, is changed

  • themes and choose fonts kittens: Fix search freezing for many seconds when typing a long query, such as the full name of a theme

  • macOS: Fix a custom dock icon reverting to the stock icon after a progress bar is cleared (#10545)

  • macOS: Fix a regression in the previous release causing background_opacity less than one with no background_blur making the titlebar transparent (#10540)

  • macOS: Fix regression in 0.49 that caused rounded rect shader to not work on ancient macs with AMD GPUs (#10549)

  • diff kitten: Fix search not finding matches at the end of a line

  • hints kitten: Fix delays of many seconds when selecting paths or line numbers on a screen with long lines that contain no spaces

  • File transfer: Fix a security issue where a malicious program on the remote machine could bypass the transfer confirmation prompt when no file_transfer_confirmation_bypass password is set

  • Fix an out-of-bounds memory access when drawing a multi-line text sized character with the cursor below the bottom margin of the scroll region

  • Fix a heap buffer underflow when parsing ANSI-C quoted strings in the command line sent by shell integration via the OSC 133 escape code

  • macOS: Fix a regression in 0.49 that caused rendering issues after wake from sleep or display re configuration under memory pressure due to a bug in Apple’s OpenGL drivers (#10571)

0.49.1 [2026-09-24]¶

  • Drag and drop: Hover over a tab while dragging a window or a single window tab to switch to it and choose a split position. Drop a window at a tab edge or gap to put it into a new tab at that position. Dragging tabs now shows an insertion marker rather than moving the other tabs during the drag. See Overview for details.

  • Splits layout: Dragging a divider now resizes only its adjacent regions, consistently after rearranging windows. Fix nested dividers not tracking mouse movement correctly, including when returning from a minimum size.

  • Splits layout: Fix windows in a nested split overlapping their neighbour by a couple of pixels when the split is resized down to its minimum size.

  • Splits layout: Fix the next split collapsing to a single line after equalizing a tab with only one window, or closing a window with equalize_on_window_close enabled (#10522)

  • icat: Fix a regression in 0.49.0 --transfer-mode=memory not displaying anything and --detect-support reporting files, because the names of the POSIX shared memory objects it created were missing the leading slash mandated by the graphics protocol (#10517)

  • Fix a packaging bug that could cause pipeline files to be omitted from some kitty builds

  • save_as_session: Show an error instead of saving next to the directory when the specified path is an existing directory (#10520)

0.49.0 [2026-09-21]¶

  • Support for Custom Shaders for adding various graphical effects (#10344)

  • Throughput performance improvements for a 15-35% real world improvement depending on workload

  • Add window_border_radius for rounded window borders (#10421)

  • A new option remap_modifiers to allow having modifier keys behave as different modifier keys (#10307)

  • A new option, padding_fill_strategy to control how the thin padding strips that appear when the window size is not an exact multiple of the cell size are colored. You can choose to have the padding colored to match the background of each neighboring cell, effectively extending the size of the cell or you can continue to use the existing behavior of using the background.

  • Splits layout: Add an optional proportional sizing policy that preserves adjusted window weights when adding, closing or repositioning windows. See Arrange windows for configuration (#10471)

  • The scrollbar option now takes a new value scrolled-or-hovered to also show the scrollbar when the mouse moves over the scrollbar region (#10345)

  • A new kitten @ screenshot remote control command to take a pixel perfect PNG screenshot of an OS Window, tab or window

  • A new kitten @ set-os-window-title remote control command to set the title for an already-open OS Window and optionally restore automatic title tracking when no title is specified

  • Wayland: Fix the first movement of the scroll wheel after reversing direction often not scrolling, with high resolution wheels such as the Logitech MX Master 3 (#10306)

  • Allow dragging selected text to other windows or applications with the mouse_selection drag_or_normal_select mouse action, in addition to its existing support for dragging links. See the configuration examples to enable it.

  • Vertical tabs: Improve handling of multi-line tab titles. Controlled via two new options: tab_title_max_lines and tab_title_template (#10303)

  • Vertical tabs: Improve rendering of tabs when using the fade tab_bar_style

  • remember_window_size now also remembers window maximized state (#10308)

  • Sessions: Also save/restore layouts other than the currently active layout (#10324)

  • Wayland: Fix clipboard sharing between kitty instances in containers with isolated PID namespaces and stale paste data when used with clipboard managers that restore application private MIME types (#10352, #10376)

  • When expanding a window in alternate screen mode use the most common background color as the color for the newly created lines leading to less visual flicker until the application can redraw itself (#10365)

  • macOS: Allow kitty OS Windows to participate in Split View tiling (#103701)

  • Allow dropping a tab containing a single window into another tab’s layout, using the existing window drop preview and preserving running programs. See Overview for details.

  • Port remaining built in kittens from Python to Go (#10371)

  • Splits layout: Fix dragging a border resizing the wrong split in nested layouts.

  • Linux: Fix drawing a screen containing many distinct codepoints that are not present in the main font causing a noticeable stall (#10496)

  • Graphics protocol: Fix scaled images (created with the r or c keys) being distorted instead of clipped when scrolled against a margin (#10377)

  • IME preedit text: use underline rather than reverse video (#10386)

  • Map mouse button presses in the padding around a window to the nearest cell, so that, for example, selections can be started by pressing in the padding. Presses in the margins and in the region around window borders used for dragging borders no longer start selections (#10393)

  • dnd kitten: Add an option to use file copies instead of hard links for copy drops (#10412)

  • Fix a malformed CSI escape sequence such as \e[?: corrupting the parser state so that subsequent SGR color codes are ignored (#10434)

  • Thai/Lao: Render the vowel sign AM (U+0E33/U+0EB3) correctly by widening the cell it combines into, matching wcwidth() based programs (#10477)

  • Text sizing protocol: A cell whose width was set explicitly with the w key is no longer narrowed by a subsequent U+FE0E variation selector

  • Fix dropping files or URLs onto a window being delivered to the wrong window, or ignored entirely, when the tab bar is at the top or on either side

  • Graphics protocol: Fix a regression in 0.45.0 that caused the overwrite composition mode for animation frames (a=f) to be controlled by the undocumented C key instead of the documented X key (#10379)

  • Graphics protocol: Fix chunked transmission of animation frame data (a=f) replacing the image’s root frame instead of creating or editing the animation frame, when the continuation chunks contain only the m key, as prescribed by the spec

  • Graphics protocol: Reduce memory usage and speed up image transmission by moving image data into the disk cache instead of copying it. Images transmitted with the transient usage hint no longer keep a redundant second copy of their data in memory for their entire lifetime

  • Graphics protocol: Fix a memory leak when transmitting an animation frame based on a frame with a long chain of references to other frames

  • Graphics protocol: Fix image data being lost or read back incorrectly in the rare case that an image was overwritten or deleted while its previous data was being written to the disk cache by the cache’s background thread

  • Drag and drop protocol: deny requests for drag data made before the user has actually dropped something onto the window (CVE 2026-80432)

  • Drag and drop protocol: Deny drag sources that send identically named symlink/dir entries with an appropriate error (CVE 2026-80430)

  • Drag and drop protocol: Fix a use-after-free when a drag source item is aborted mid-transfer, where the freed remote item was still read from and written to after the drag offer was torn down (CVE 2026-95834)

  • Text sizing protocol: Fix a buffer overflow when a natural width text sizing escape code contains a grapheme cluster longer than four codepoints (CVE 2026-80431)

  • ssh kitten askpass: Verify owner and permissions of SHM memory used for askpass (CVE 2026-95835)

  • Graphics protocol: Fix a crash when transmitting image data via a file or shared memory object (t=f, t=t or t=s) and the client truncates it while kitty is reading from it.

  • Graphics protocol: Fix reading image data from a file or shared memory object at an offset (the O key) failing unless the offset happened to be a multiple of the system page size

  • Graphics protocol: Fix file descriptor leak that can be triggered by malicious clients

  • Graphics protocol: Make fileopen failure responses generic to avoid leaking any information about failed files

  • edit-in-kitty: harden the code used to parse messages from clients

  • Linux: kitty --single-instance: Only accept commands from processes running as the same user

  • Clipboard protocol: Report an EFBIG error to programs that try to write more data to the clipboard than allowed by clipboard_max_size, instead of silently truncating their data. Also fix clipboard_max_size being interpreted in units of TB rather than MB (#10399)

  • Color control protocol: Report unknown fields as unknown=<base64 encoded field name> instead of echoing the field name back verbatim, which allowed using the escape code to make the terminal emit arbitrary printable ASCII text (CVE 2026-95832)

  • macOS: Fix dropping files that are provided as file promises pasting paths to files that no longer exist. The dropped files are now kept alive for ten minutes and removed when kitty quits (#10430)

  • macOS: Fix all signal handling being permanently disabled after the first window that used the graphics protocol is closed. This caused exited window shells to accumulate as zombie processes and also broke reloading the config with SIGUSR1 and quitting on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP (#10436)

  • macOS: Fix long text from input methods being discarded when committed outside a key event (#10468)

  • Multiple cursors protocol: Fix hiding the main cursor with DECTCEM also hiding the extra cursors (#10489)

  • Add a new passthrough_and_end value for the --on-unknown option of map, that passes the unknown key through to the program and also exits the custom keyboard mode (#10490)

  • macOS: Allow input methods to read the text around the cursor, so that input methods that automatically insert a space between Latin and CJK text work (#10492)

0.48.2 [2026-07-30]¶

  • Wayland: Fix regression in previous release that broke drag and drop on Plasma (#10284)

  • diff kitten: Fix a rare crash when showing a large diff due to incorrect locking when highlighting

  • Allow the private DCS kitty-echo escape code to only echo numbers (CVE 2026-72913)

  • Linux: Fix an approx 1MB memory leak when reloading the config, introduced in version 0.40.0 (#10290)

  • Desktop file chooser integration: when the specified directory does not exist, open file chooser at home directory (#10292)

  • Add support for terminal visibility reports

  • tab_title_template: Add a field that evaluates to the total memory used by all child processes in the tab (#10293)

0.48.1 [2026-07-24]¶

  • Wayland: fix a regression in the previous release that broke window sizing for on Hyprland/Sway with fractional scales and an initial specified size (#10268)

  • Wayland: fix a regression in 0.47.3 that broke dragging on the Niri compositor (#10271)

  • Wayland: get initial window size in cells working in most cases on Hyprland/Sway with fractional scaling by using the fractional scale of the primary monitor

  • Wayland: fix using remote control to resize OS windows on some tiling compositors leading to broken rendering

  • macOS: fix edge=none panel height shrinking when margin_top is non-zero in the panel/quick-access-terminal kittens (#10278)

0.48.0 [2026-07-18]¶

  • Implement vertical tabs by setting tab_bar_edge to left or right (#9855)

  • Graphics protocol: Add a new transient usage hint that clients can send to terminals to indicate an image is meant for only short duration use (#10092)

  • On first press in an unfocused OS Window/kitty window give it focus and pass the mouse event through to the clicked element. This is a behavior change but aligns with platform defaults on macOS. Linux has no platform defaults here as far as I can tell, so it gets to follow along. (#10233)

  • kitten @ get-text: Add support for alternate and alternate_scrollback extents to fetch text from the alternate screen buffer (#10165)

  • Wayland: Fix first OS window being a few cells too small when initial_window_width/initial_window_height are set in cells and a fractional display scale is in use (#10146)

  • macOS: New option macos_ns_window_layer to more precisely control what layer panel OS windows are placed on (#10116)

  • macOS: New option macos_use_physical_screen_frame to allow panel OS Windows to cover the macOS global dock bar (#10116)

  • kitty binary builds are now built on Ubuntu 22 upgraded from Ubuntu 18 for improved performance from better compilers

  • macOS: Fix incorrect horizontal alignment when using text sizing protocol (#10179)

  • edit-in-kitty: Return exit code from underlying editor process on exit (#10198)

  • Make erasing last command robust against commands with no output and commands in the scrollback (#10201)

  • Fix superfluous margin visible to the left and right of the tab bar when background_opacity is less than one and the window width is not a multiple of the cell width (#10212)

  • hints kitten: Add a new flag kitty +kitten hints --prefix-free to generate hints without a shared prefix (#10210)

  • Wayland GNOME: Fix dragging a window title bar to the “+” button failing to create a new tab when there is only a single tab (#10222)

  • choose-files kitten: Add a --mode=all to select either an existing file or directory (#10208)

  • Add support for editing files in sublime text and zed at specified line number (#10224)

  • choose-file kitten: Use a full readline editor for the search box. Also allow remapping the up/down/home/end keys to use for editing instead of navigating the file list (#10225)

  • Fix remote_control_script not working in a kitty instance run from inside another kitty instance

  • quick-access-terminal kitten: Allow configuring the layer on which to display the terminal (#10242)

  • cursor_trail_start_threshold now optionally accepts two values to set x (horizontal) and y (vertical) thresholds independently (#10246)

  • scroll-window remote control command: Fix a regression that broke scrolling by pages (#10253)

  • Bypass libc malloc for history buffer to avoid libc pool policies causing apparent memory leak (#10254)

  • Cursor trail: Do not run the trail shader when the cursor is hidden, saving resources (#10255)

  • Graphics: Fix incorrect calculated cursor position when placing images with X/Y cell offsets (#10256)

  • macOS: Disable macOS one time code autofill popups (#10250)

  • Add support for DECSTR soft screen reset escape code (#10263)

  • macOS: Fix quick-access-terminal appearing on the wrong space (the fullscreen app’s space) when triggered from a different space on macOS Tahoe (#8740)

0.47.4 [2026-06-15]¶

  • Linux: Fix a regression in the previous release that broke rendering of bitmap color fonts (#10145)

  • Linux: Allow fake italics defined via a matrix in fontconfig settings to work for fonts like Fira Code that do not ship with an italic face (#10120)

0.47.3 [2026-06-12]¶

  • macOS: Show a key symbol on the active tab if the macOS Secure Input feature is enabled

  • Fix regression that broke unserialization of splits layout in previous release (#10124)

  • Fix focus_follows_mouse switching the active window when returning to a desktop/space, even though the mouse did not move. Now the window under a stationary cursor is left alone, while moving the mouse across windows still switches focus as before.

  • Sanitise responses to color control escape codes to avoid command injection for shells that do not use the kitty keyboard protocol (CVE 2026-54057)

  • choose fonts kitten: Fix a rare timing based race causing kitten to crash at startup (#10128)

  • Wayland: Fix mouse input getting broken when starting a tab drag and releasing the mouse button before the drag is actually registered (#10136)

0.47.2 [2026-06-07]¶

  • Allow dragging to move scrollbar after clicking on track when scrollbar_jump_on_click is enabled (#10085)

  • macOS: Fix regression in 0.47.0 that broke passing Cmd+C on to terminal applications when no text is selected (#10087)

  • kitten @ set-background-image: Fix --layout=configured changing layout to centered instead (#10089)

  • Splits layout: add an equalize action and an equalize_on_window_close option to redistribute split space proportionally (#3489)

  • Fix matching var/env on tabs not working as expected (#10095)

  • When watching for changed config files do not recursively watch all sub directories of the directory containing the config file (#10102)

  • File transfer protocol: use O_NOFOLLOW when opening regular files (CVE 2026-54055)

  • dnd kitten: Protect against drops from malicious sources (CVE 2026-54056)

0.47.1 [2026-05-28]¶

  • Fix a regression in the previous release that caused copy_or_noop to stop working correctly (#10041)

  • macOS: Fix a regression in the previous release that caused URLs to be quoted when dropping into shells (#10054)

  • Fix a regression in the previous release that broke automatic color scheme changes when using a background image (#10058)

  • Fix auto_reload_config not working when kitty.conf is a symlink (#10066)

  • Fix a regression in the previous release that broke dragging of URLs to the shell prompt from programs that dont support MOVE drag operations

  • Preserve user-set tab stops across window resizes instead of resetting to 8 column default

  • Add support for the DECST8C escape sequence (CSI ? 5 W) to reset tab stops to every 8 columns

  • X11: Fix panel/quick-access-terminal windows not staying on top under KDE after they are hidden once (#10082)

0.47.0 [2026-05-19]¶

  • A new Drag and drop kitten to allow drag and drop of files from your shell to any GUI program even across SSH (#9984)

  • A new option palette_generate to automatically generate the 256 color palette from the first 16 colors (#9426)

  • For builtin key mappings automatically fallback to matching the US-PC layout key when the pressed key has no matches and is a non-English character (#9671)

  • Allow drag and drop of windows to re-arrange them, move them to another tab/OS Window or detach them into a new OS Window. See toggle_window_title_bars to temporarily show window title bars to drag them around (#9626)

  • Have scroll_line_up and scroll_line_down smooth scroll by default. Can be restored to old behavior by re-mapping without the smooth argument (#9689)

  • Draw a progress bar at the top of the window when a program reports progress using the OSC 9;4 escape sequence, controlled by progress_bar (#9777)

  • Automatically reload configuration on changes, controlled by auto_reload_config

  • Allow specifying multiple background images for background_image that are stored on GPU to allow fast image switching (#9836)

  • Remote control: Expose session_name and last_focused_at in the output of kitten @ ls for each window (#9732, #9799)

  • Allow optionally dragging URLs with the mouse, see left (#9804)

  • Change focus_follows_mouse to switch the active window only when the mouse crosses into a different window, instead of on every mouse motion event. Prevents accidental mouse bumps from undoing a keyboard-driven window switch.

  • Wayland: Use hold gestures to cancel momentum scrolling when fingers are placed on the trackpad, for a more natural kinetic scrolling experience (#9863)

  • macOS: Switch to new Tahoe style application icon with different background in light and dark modes

  • Fix thickness of diagonal lines in box drawing characters not the same as horizontal/vertical lines (#9719)

  • Graphics protocol: Fix crash when handling invalid PNG image with direct transmission (CVE 2026-33633)

  • Graphics protocol: Fix crash when handling invalid offset values in graphics compose commands (CVE 2026-33642)

  • X11: Fix a regression in the previous release that caused an occasional crash on input device removal (#9723)

  • XWayland: Fix a regression where some wheel mice were not scrolling properly (#9770)

  • Command palette: Improve searching to use word level matching (#9727)

  • hints kitten: A new option to set the background color of matched text (#9745)

  • The show_hyperlink_targets option now allows specifying a keyboard modifier so that target URLs are only shown on hover when the modifier is pressed (#9741)

  • Fix a spurious mouse button release event being sent when dragging out of an OS window causes focus loss

  • Fix scrollbar hover/interaction not working when the scrollbar is drawn in the window margin area (#9756)

  • Fix completion for edit-in-kitty not including some common text file types

  • Allow holding the Alt key and triple-clicking to select from the first cell even if it is empty (#9758)

  • Fix double click to rename tab being triggered too easily (#9774)

  • Fix a crash when user tries to select while the client program is using synchronised rendering and generating large amounts of output (#9778)

  • macOS: Add Copy and Paste menu items to the Edit menu in the global menu bar (#9780)

  • Fix dragging of splits layout borders sometimes moving in the wrong direction or having no effect (#9447)

  • Fix triple-click line selection and double-click word selection not extending wrapped lines beyond the edges of the viewport

  • Password input in kittens: hide the cursor and display a blinking 🔒 at the end of typed characters to make it visually clear the user is entering a password

  • edit-in-kitty: Ignore environment variables as some editors execute code present in env vars. Similarly ignore conf file specifications for colors (CVE 2026-42851)

  • Command palette ctrl+shift+f3: nicer grouping of aliases and combined actions (#9819)

  • hints kitten: Fix trailing punctuation not being removed from URLs (#9828)

  • Fix copy/paste dropping spaces at soft-wrap boundaries when strip_trailing_spaces is set (#9834)

  • Allow setting negative values for inactive_text_alpha to control whether to only fade inactive windows or unfocused windows (#9837)

  • A new option macos_fullscreen_ignore_safe_area_insets to control whether to ignore the notch space when using macos_traditional_fullscreen (#9841)

  • Fix some responses from terminal sometimes leaking into shell after kitten exit (#9839)

  • Render block elements from the Unicode Symbols for Legacy Computing Supplement block (U+1CC00–U+1CEBF): separated block quadrants, separated block sextants, one sixteenth blocks, and one quarter block partial fills (#9849)

  • Improve performance of using active process data when rendering the tab bar by only scanning processes once per second (#9862)

  • macOS: Fix occasional phantom cursors being drawn on screen (#9725)

  • diff kitten: Keep the current (topmost) filename visible when scrolling, controlled by a new option kitten-diff.sticky_header (#9891)

  • Add an option to focus_follows_mouse to only switch focus on drops rather than movement (#9896)

  • Fix setting momentum_scroll to zero not fully disabling momentum scrolling (#9904)

  • macOS: Fix args passed via open --args being ignored when macos-launch-services-cmdline is present (#9910)

  • save_as_session: when the filename input by the user has no extension, automatically add the .kitty-session extension (#9919)

  • Linux: Workaround bug in Nvidia drivers that caused color corruption when resuming after suspend (#9844)

  • choose-files kitten: Output a trailing newline when writing to a tty in text format (#9982)

  • ssh kitten: Sanitize user controlled data in error messages that might leak to shell (CVE 2026-42850)

  • Linux: Respect the fontconfig matrix setting commonly used for fake slant with fonts that do not have italic variants (#9990)

0.46.2 [2026-03-21]¶

  • Watchers: Add an on_quit event to global watchers (#9675)

  • Wayland: Fix a crash on some compositors when dragging a tab between OS Windows (#9677)

  • Fix incorrect behavior when using the actions to move tab forward/backward with a tab_bar_filter active (#9672)

  • Prevent stacking of multiple rename tab windows (#9691)

  • choose files kitten: Fix a regression that caused incorrect highlight of matched letters

  • macOS: When using macos_traditional_fullscreen do not render content under the notch (#9678)

  • X11: Fix massive scroll when switching focus between kitty and another application (#9703)

  • Markers: Fix marking not working for multicell characters (#9705)

0.46.1 [2026-03-16]¶

  • diff kitten: Highlight moved lines using a different background color (kitten-diff.mark_moved_lines) (#3241)

  • Fix a regression that broke kitten update-self (#9642)

  • macOS: Clear bell alert badge on dock icon on mouse/keyboard activity (#9640)

  • Fix a regression that broke accept anyway shortcut in the paste confirmation dialog (#9640)

  • Fix kitty hanging on startup on Intel macs (#9643)

  • X11: Fix a regression that caused some high res scroll devices to be treated as line based scroll devices (#9649)

  • Wayland: Fix momentum scrolling not working on compositors that send a stop frame with no axis information (#9653)

  • Linux: momentum scrolling in the kitty scrollback buffer for touchpads and touchscreens, see momentum_scroll

  • X11: support high resolution scroll events from touchpads, etc

  • Allow dragging tabs (opt:drag_threshold) in the tab bar to re-order, move to another OS Window or detach (#9296)

  • Allow showing configurable window titles for individual kitty windows via a window title bar (#9450)

  • choose-files kitten: Fix JXL image preview not working (#9323)

  • Fix tab bar rendering glitches when using tab_bar_filter in some circumstances (#9328)

  • Add support for specifying colors in kitty.conf in OKLCH and LAB color spaces (#9325)

  • Fix a regression that broke using line numbers with the edit-in-kitty command (#9346)

  • Wayland: Remove usage of the Wayland color management protocol to inform compositors of the color space used by kitty (#9341)

  • Linux: Fix a regression in 0.40 that caused horizontal alignment for emoji to be incorrect in some cases (#9395)

  • kitten @: Fix relative paths for --password-file being resolved relative to CWD instead of the kitty config directory

  • kitten choose-files: Add a new binding of Alt+Enter to modify the name of an existing file when choosing a save file name (#9387)

  • kitten choose-files: Fix TAB completion in the choose save file name prompt not working with respect to the current working directory (#9387)

  • Fix line-at-once selection not extending wrapped lines into scrollback (#9437)

  • ssh kitten: Restore keyboard mode even if the ssh connection drops

  • macOS: Fix changing window title with global menubar menu open causes menu to get stuck (#9490)

  • Fix focus_follows_mouse not working during a drag and drop (#9497)

  • goto_session: Add a --active-only option to select from only active sessions (#9503)

  • Shell integration: Allow sending click events to shells using y co-ordinates relative to prompts (#9500)

  • A new action copy_selection_or_last_command_output (#9512)

  • URL detection: Allow trailing asterisks in URLs (#9543)

  • Text sizing protocol: Fix alignment/cropping issues when rendering text with a fractional scale (#9471)

  • macOS: Fix a crash when using macos_traditional_fullscreen with split view (#9573)

  • macOS: Fix flickering during OS Window resize (#9582)

  • Cursor trail: Show a cursor trail when switching tabs (#9588)

  • Make shift+left click extend the current selection instead of starting a new selection when the mouse is not grabbed by the TUI application (#9608)

  • Allow double clicking on a tab to rename it (#9609)

  • remote_control_script resolve relative paths with respect to kitty config directory (#9625)

0.45.0 [2025-12-24]¶

  • A new kitten to select files at the speed of thought with a keyboard first interface and support for content previews of text files with syntax highlighting, images, videos, e-books and more (#9263)

  • Add support for the paste events protocol (#9183)

  • Wayland: Fix spurious key repeat events when some user defined callback takes a long time to execute (#9224)

  • When moving windows to a new tab/OS Window fix overlay windows not being grouped with their parent windows (#9266)

  • Linux: Fix a bug causing colors to occasionally all go black when using mesa >= 25.3.0 with nouveau GPU driver (#9235)

  • Fix tab_bar_min_tabs not respecting tab_bar_filter (#9278)

  • macOS: Workaround for regression in Tahoe 26.2 that breaks kitty --detach (#9288)

  • macOS: Workaround for yet another Tahoe regression causing macOS to start an AutoFill helper process and not shut it down on application exit (#9299)

0.44.0 [2025-11-03]¶

  • Allow kitty to read a specified set of environment variables from your login shell at startup using the env directive in kitty.conf (#9042)

  • A new option draw_window_borders_for_single_window to force kitty to always draw a window border even when only a single window is present (#9112)

  • Fix a regression in 0.43.0 that caused a black flicker when closing a tab in the presence of a background image (#9060)

  • Further improvements to rounded corner rendering, especially at low DPI (#9091)

  • Splits layout: Fix a bug that could cause a corrupted layout in some circumstances (#9059)

  • Fix a regression in the previous release that broke goto_session -1

  • Fix tab bar sometimes showing incorrect tabs when it is filtered to show only tabs from the current session (#9079)

  • Graphics: Fix animated images sometimes not auto playing or auto playing at the wrong start frame if the same image id is used for a subsequent image

  • Fix a regression in 0.43.0 that caused high CPU usage when disable_ligatures was set to cursor and the tab bar was visible (#9071)

  • macOS: Handle dropping of file promises into kitty in addition to file paths (#9084)

  • macOS: Fix indeterminate progress bar displayed on dock icon increasing speed when indeterminate progress is set without being cleared first (#9114)

  • macOS: Performance and power usage improvements of about 5-10% (#9131)

  • macOS: Add an item to the global menu to Cycle through OS windows

  • macOS: Quick access terminal: Fix a crash when changing font size (#9178)

  • Wayland: Fix center-sized panels not working on smithay based compositors (#9117)

  • Wayland: Fix scrolling using some mouse wheels that produce “VALUE120” based scroll events too fast on some compositors (#9128)

  • Add support for Unicode 17

  • Fix a regression in 0.43.0 that caused tab_bar_margin_width to be doubled on the right edge of the tab bar (#9154)

  • Session files: Add a new focus_tab command to specify which tab should be active when a session is loaded. Accepts either a plain number (0-based index) or a match expression for flexible tab selection, allowing sessions to preserve the active tab state (Sessions)

  • save_as_session: Add --base-dir option to specify a base directory for saving session files with relative paths, useful when the current working directory is not the desired location (Sessions)

  • Add state:focused_os_window match query to select all windows in the currently focused OS window (Matching windows and tabs)

  • Session saving now preserves visual tab order and active tab rather than tab activation history as this is generally more important. In the future may have it save tab history as well (#9163)

  • The ctrl+shift+delete shortcut to reset the terminal now also resets termios state

0.43.1 [2025-10-01]¶

  • ssh kitten: Allow specifying a password and/or TOTP authentication secret to automate interactive logins in scenarios where public key authentication is not supported (#9020)

  • macOS: Fix a bug where the color of a transparent titlebar was off when running in the release build versus the build from source. Also fix using a transparent titlebar causing the background opacity to be doubled.

  • Fix a regression in the previous release that caused the incorrect tab to be active when loading a session (#9025)

  • macOS: Workaround for bug in macOS Tahoe that caused closed OS Windows to remain as invisible rectangles that intercept mouse events (#8952)

  • macOS: Fix a regression in the previous release that broke automatic switching of dark/light mode when setting macos_titlebar_color to an arbitrary color (#9034)

  • goto_session: Add --sort-by=alphabetical to have the interactive session picker list the sessions in a fixed order rather than by most recent (#9033)

  • Fix a regression in the previous release that caused the cursor trail to not be hidden properly (#9039)

  • Session files: Fix a regression in the previous release that broke matching on windows in the current tab (#9037)

  • Fix a regression in the previous release that broke clearing screen lines when in margin mode (#9049)

0.43.0 [2025-09-28]¶

  • New support for creating and switching to Sessions easily, allowing users to define and use sessions/projects efficiently (#8911)

  • Add a configurable scrollbar for the kitty scrollback (#8945)

  • A new protocol for multiple cursors in the terminal (#8927)

  • macOS: Allow the window title bar to be semi-transparent when background_opacity is less than one and macos_titlebar_color is set to background (#8906)

  • A new cursor_trail_color setting to independently control the color of cursor trails (#8830)

  • macOS: Add the default Cmd+L mapping from Terminal.app to erase the last command and its output (#6040)

  • Fix background_opacity being non-linear especially with light color themes. Note that this might require you to adjust the value of this setting to get back your current look. (#8869)

  • backward incompatibility: background_opacity no longer applies to background_image instead add an alpha channel to the image itself

  • Add support for blinking text. Text marked as blinking now blinks in exact rhythm with the cursor. The blinking animation and max duration are controlled by cursor_blink_interval and cursor_stop_blinking_after. (#8551)

  • Allow using a custom python function to draw tab titles in the tab bar, see tab_title_template

  • Wayland: Fix incorrect window size calculation when transitioning from full screen to non-full screen with client side decorations (#8826)

  • macOS: Fix hiding quick access terminal window not restoring focus to previously active application (#8840)

  • macOS: Fix showing the quick access terminal on a space other than the space it was last active on, after full screening some application causes the quick access terminal to appear on the old space (#8740)

  • macOS: When toggling open the quick access terminal move it to the currently active monitor (the monitor with the mouse pointer on it) (#9003)

  • macOS: Fix closing an OS Window when another OS Window is minimized causing the minimized window to be un-minimized (#8913)

  • Allow using backspace to move the cursor onto the previous line in cooked mode. This is indicated by the bw property in kitty’s terminfo (#8841)

  • Watchers: A new event for global watchers corresponding to the tab bar being changed (#8842)

  • Fix a regression in 0.40.0 that broke handling of the VS16 variation selector when it caused a character to flow to the next line (#8848)

  • Fix rendering of underlines when using larger text sizes with the space and en-space characters (#8950)

  • Fix updating panel configuration on visibility toggle and via remote control not working (#8984)

  • Improve rendering of rounded rectangles (#9000)

  • Wayland: Update bundled copy of libwayland to 1.24 from 1.23.1 because the just released mesa 25.2.0 breaks with libwayland < 1.24 (#8884)

  • macOS: Pass the Cmd+C shortcut to the application running in the terminal when no text is selected (#8946)

  • macOS: Workaround for bug in macOS Tahoe that caused OS Windows that are fullscreen on a monitor that is disconnected while macOS is asleep to crash kitty (#8983)

0.42.2 [2025-07-16]¶

  • A new protocol extension to notify terminal programs that have turned on SGR Pixel mouse reporting when the mouse leaves the window (#8808)

  • clipboard kitten: Can now optionally take a password to avoid repeated permission prompts when accessing the clipboard. Based on a protocol extension. (#8789)

  • A new launch --hold-after-ssh to not close a launched window that connects directly to a remote host because of launch --cwd=current when the connection ends (#8807)

  • Fix remember_window_position not working because of a stupid typo (#8646)

  • A new kitty --grab-keyboard that can be used to grab the keyboard so that global shortcuts are sent to kitty instead

  • Remote control: Fix holding a remote control socket open causing the kitty I/O thread to go into a loop and not respond on other remote control sockets (#8670)

  • hints kitten: Preserve line breaks when the hint is over a line break (#8674)

  • Fix a segfault when using the copy_ansi_to_clipboard action (#8682)

  • Fix a crash when using linear easing curves for animations (#8692)

  • Graphics protocol: Add a note clarifying image update behavior on re-transmission (#8701)

  • Wayland GNOME: Fix incorrect OS Window tracking because GNOME has started activating windows on non-current workspaces (#8716)

  • Fix a regression in 0.40.0 that broke rendering of VS15 variation selectors in some circumstances (#8731, #8794)

  • Fix a regression in 0.40.0 that broke serialization of tab characters as ANSI text (#8741)

  • Fix a regression in 0.40.0 that broke erasing of characters in a line in the presence of wide characters (#8758)

  • Fix a regression in 0.40.0 that broke hyperlinking of wide characters (#8796)

  • Fix a regression that broke using esc to exit visual select window mode (#8767)

  • kitten run-shell: Fix SIGINT blocked when execing the shell (#8754)

0.42.1 [2025-05-17]¶

  • Fix ambiguous width and private use characters not being rendered when used with variable width text-sizing protocol escape codes

  • Quick access terminal: Restore focus to previously active window when hiding the quick access terminal window on macOS (#8627)

  • Wayland: Fix an abort if the terminal program sets a window title longer than 2KB that contains CSI escape sequences and multibyte UTF-8 (#8619)

  • Quick access terminal: Allow toggling the window to full screen using the standard kitty ctrl+shift+f11 shortcut (#8626)

  • Quick access terminal: Allow configuring the monitor to display the panel on in Wayland/X11 (#8630)

  • A new setting remember_window_position to optionally use the position of the last closed kitty OS Window as the position of the first kitty OS Window when running a new kitty instance (#8601)

  • Panel kitten: A new center-sized value for --edge to allow easily creating sized and centered panels

  • Wayland: The kitty --name flag now sets the XDG window tag on compositors that support the xdg-toplevel-tag protocol.

0.42.0 [2025-05-11]¶

  • A new kitten: quick-access-terminal to Make a Quake like quick access terminal

  • The panel kitten works on macOS and X11 as well as Wayland (#2590)

  • Behavior change: Now kitty does full grapheme segmentation following the Unicode 16 spec when splitting text into cells (#8533)

  • Behavior change: The automatic color switching functionality now also controls background image settings (#8603)

  • panel kitten: Allow using kitty +kitten panel --single-instance to create multiple panels in one process (#8549)

  • launch: Allow creating desktop panels such as those created by the panel kitten (#8549)

  • Remote control: Allow modifying desktop panels and showing/hiding OS Windows using the kitten @ resize-os-window command (#8550)

  • Remote control launch: Allow waiting for a program launched in a new window to exit and get the exit code via the kitty +launch --wait-for-child-to-exit command line flag (#8573)

  • Allow starting kitty with the OS window hidden via kitty --start-as=hidden, useful for single instance mode (#3466)

  • Allow configuring the mouse unhide behavior when using mouse_hide_wait (#8508)

  • diff kitten: Add half page and full page scroll vim-like bindings (#8514)

  • diff kitten: Allow diffing named pipes (#8597)

  • Fix a regression that caused automatic color themes to not be re-applied after config file reload (#8530)

  • Wayland: When the compositor supports the xdg-system-bell protocol use it to play the default bell sound

  • panel kitten: Allow specifying panel size in pixels in addition to cells

  • Fix a regression in 0.36.0 that caused using = with single letter command line flags to no longer work correctly (#8556)

  • Single instance: Preserve environment variables from invoking environment in newly created window (#8567)

  • Single instance: Reset OS Window class and name in new single instance OS windows (#8567)

  • macOS: Fix text color in visual window select ignoring the color theme (#8579)

  • Launch action: Allow using an env var that resolves to a full command-line as the program to launch (#8613)

  • change_font_size allow multiplying/dividing the current font size in addition to incrementing it (#8616)

  • Box drawing: Improve appearance of rounder corners, giving them a uniform line width (#8299)

0.41.1 [2025-04-03]¶

  • Fix a regression in the previous release that caused rendering of emoji using the VS16 variation selector to fail with some fonts (#8495)

  • Fix a regression in 0.40.0 that caused tab bar margins to not be properly blanked when the tab bar is at the bottom (#8494)

  • Wayland: panel kitten: Fix incorrect initial font size on compositors such as Hyprland that set scale late in the window creation process (#8496)

  • Fix a regression in 0.40.1 that caused hyperlink underline on hover to remain on screen when the screen is scrolled

0.41.0 [2025-03-29]¶
